text_blocks.snippet: CRE (Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae) is primarily spread through direct or indirect contact with infected or colonized individuals in healthcare settings. This often involves contact with wounds or stool from infected or colonized individuals. CRE can also be transmitted through contaminated surfaces or medical equipment.
snippet_highlighted_words: primarily spread through direct or indirect contact with infected or colonized individuals in healthcare settings

list.title: Direct contact:
list.snippet: This includes contact with bodily fluids like blood, wound drainage, urine, stool, or sputum from an infected or colonized person, according to the New Mexico Department of Health.

list.title: Indirect contact:
list.snippet: This involves touching contaminated surfaces or equipment, such as doorknobs, bedrails, or medical devices, that have been touched by an infected or colonized individual.

list.title: Healthcare settings:
list.snippet: CRE is most commonly spread in hospitals and other healthcare facilities where there is close contact with patients, medical devices, and potentially contaminated surfaces.

list.title: Colonization:
list.snippet: People can also be colonized with CRE, meaning they carry the bacteria but don't show symptoms of infection. These individuals can still transmit the bacteria to others, according to the Wisconsin Department of Health Services.

list.title: Not airborne or casual contact:
list.snippet: CRE is not spread through the air or through casual contact like hugging or shaking hands.
